text: Write a story called The Secret. In your writing, create a sense of drama and anticipation.
Write two contrasting diary entries (300–450 words each). The first is by a young person who has
just tried a new activity for the first time; the second is by the same person, now older, who has
just won a major prize for this activity. In your writing, create a sense of the person’s outlook and
mood.
Write a descriptive piece called The Playground. In your writing, focus on colour, sound and
movement to help your reader imagine the scene.
Section B: Writing for an audience
In class, you have been discussing reasons for learning about the history of your country. Write
an article for your school magazine, in which you describe the benefits of studying history. In your
writing, create a sense of the importance of history and an enthusiasm for learning about the past.
Two students are going to take part in a debate on computer games. One of the students believes
that playing computer games is good for you, and the other student feels they are harmful. Write
the texts of their speeches (300–450 words each).
An environmental organisation has produced a short video to raise awareness of the need to
protect the environment. Write the voiceover script for this video. In your writing, create a sense of
the importance of being environmentally friendly.
